## The Grammar of Graphics

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}

* **data**: dataset that contains the data

* **geom**: geometric shape that the data are mapped to
    + point, line, bar, text, ...
    
* **aes**thetic: visual properties of the **geom** 
    + x position, y position, color, fill, shape
    
* **coord**: coordinate system
    + Cartesian, polar, geographic
    
* **scale**: controls how data are mapped to the visual values of the aesthetic
    + EX: particular colors, linear

* **guide**: legend to help user convert visual display back to the data    

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r, out.width = "100%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
include_graphics("img/layers.png") 
```

:::

::::

## Choices

For most data, there won't be just **one** way to graph it. Decisions to be made:


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='45%'}

* What **geom** to use
    + Point, line, bar, ...
    
* For a given geom, how to map variables to its **aesthetics**
    + Size, location, color, ...

:::

::: {.column width='10%'}

:::

::: {.column width='45%'}


* For each **aesthetic**, what scale to use
    + Linear, diverging colors, ...
    
* For the graph, what **coordinate system** to use
    + Cartesian, polar


:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

Let's discuss some considerations that can help guide these decisions.  But...

:::


::: {.fragment}

> "Data visualization is part art and part science. The challenge is to get the art right without getting the science wrong and vice versa." -- Claus Wilke

:::

::: {.fragment}

**Recommendation:** Try out different options and make sure to iterate!

:::

## Consideration: Consider variable type when picking the aesthetic mapping.

Some aesthetics are ordinal.  Some are not.  Some can be both!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='40%'}

* Color palettes, for example, can be:
    + **Sequential**: Ordered data with one direction
    + **Diverging**: Ordered data with two directions
    + **Qualitative**: No order to the data

:::

::: {.column width='60%'}

```{r, out.width = "100%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
include_graphics("img/cb_palettes.001.jpeg") 
```

:::

## Consideration: Consider variable type when picking the aesthetic mapping.

Our ability to perceive differences varies by aesthetic!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
math241_form <- read_csv("data/Background Survey for Math 241_ Data Science (Responses) - Form Responses 1.csv") %>%
  rename(ggplot2 = `For each R package or activity, rate what you think your proficiency level is. (For many of these, I am guessing the answer is "No experience" and that is completely fine!) [ggplot2]`,
         dplyr = `For each R package or activity, rate what you think your proficiency level is. (For many of these, I am guessing the answer is "No experience" and that is completely fine!) [dplyr]`,
         tidyr = `For each R package or activity, rate what you think your proficiency level is. (For many of these, I am guessing the answer is "No experience" and that is completely fine!) [tidyr]`) %>%
  mutate(ggplot2 = forcats::fct_relevel(ggplot2,
                                        "No experience",
                                        "Limited experience",
                                        "Moderate experience",
                                        "Expert")) %>%
  mutate(dplyr = forcats::fct_relevel(dplyr,
                                        "No experience",
                                        "Limited experience",
                                        "Moderate experience",
                                        "Expert"))

ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#A71F69", color = "white") +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:12)
```

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
math241_form %>%
  count(ggplot2) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width=1) +
  coord_polar("y", start=0)   +
  theme_void() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d()
```

:::

::::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Consideration: Pick the aesthetic that makes it easy to assess value.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}

**Generally, humans are good at making comparisons involving:**

* Position
* Length
* Angle (but less so than position and length!)

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

**Generally, humans are NOT good at making comparisons involving:**

* Area (especially with irregular shapes)
* Volume
* Color shade
* Color hue

:::

::::

------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Consideration: [Respect the principle of proportional ink.](https://patient.info/news-and-features/whats-the-average-height-for-men)

**Principle of proportional ink:** The size of shaded areas need to be proportional to the data values they represent.

```{r, out.width = "40%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
include_graphics("img/men_height.png") 
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Consideration: [Respect the principle of proportional ink.](https://www.businessinsider.com/the-top-10-most-read-books-in-the-world-infographic-2012-12)

**Principle of proportional ink:** The size of shaded areas need to be proportional to the data values they represent.

```{r, out.width = "35%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
include_graphics("img/books.png") 
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Bars on a linear scale should start at 0.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Consideration: [Respect the principle of proportional ink.](https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/how-you-view-climate-change-might-depend-on-where-you-live/) 

Difficult to respect with spatial data.  Why?

```

- [Land doesn't vote, people do.](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/0e636a652d44484b9457f953994b212b)

## Consideration: [Respect the principle of proportional ink.](https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/gop-house-2022/) 

Instead of using geographic boundaries, pick a standardized shape and place "near" geographic location.

```

## Consideration: [Simplify as much as you can.](https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/ted-cruzs-general-election-strategy-is-wishful-thinking/)

## Consideration: Simplify as much as you can. {.smaller}

::: {.nonincremental}

* Over-plotting is very common in the Age of Big Data!

* Example from my own work with the US Forest Inventory and Analysis Program

:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
dat <- readRDS(url("https://mcconvil.github.io/fia_workshop_2021/data/IDdata.rds","rb"))
idaho_plots <- dat$pltassgn
ggplot(data = idaho_plots, mapping = aes(x = elev, y = BA_TPA_ADJ)) +
  geom_point() + labs(x = "Elevation", y = "Basal Area of Trees (sq ft)", caption = "Sampled Forest Inventory plots in Idaho 2011 - 2020")
``` 

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = idaho_plots, mapping = aes(x = elev, y = BA_TPA_ADJ)) +
  geom_jitter() + labs(x = "Elevation", y = "Basal Area of Trees (sq ft)", caption = "Sampled Forest Inventory plots in Idaho 2011 - 2020")
```

* Jitter the points.

:::

:::

::::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Consideration: Simplify as much as you can. {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%' .nonincremental}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = idaho_plots, mapping = aes(x = elev, y = BA_TPA_ADJ)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) + labs(x = "Elevation", y = "Basal Area of Trees (sq ft)", caption = "Sampled Forest Inventory plots in Idaho 2011 - 2020")
``` 

* Add transparency.

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = idaho_plots, mapping = aes(x = elev, y = BA_TPA_ADJ)) +
  geom_bin2d() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + labs(x = "Elevation", y = "Basal Area of Trees (sq ft)", caption = "Sampled Forest Inventory plots in Idaho 2011 - 2020")
```

* Bin the data and then try a different `geom`.

:::

:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

**Pros and cons of different approaches?**

:::

## Consideration: Make your graphs accessible!

::: {.nonincremental}

* Color contrast also matters.  
    + Shoot for a ratio of 4.5 or higher between overlapping colors.

:::

```{r, fig.width = 10, echo = FALSE, fig.asp=.4}
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#A71F69", color = "white") +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip()

p2 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#A4DBE8") +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip()
p1 + p2
```

:::: {.columns .fragment}

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r}
library(coloratio)
cr_get_ratio("#A71F69", "#EBEBEB")
```

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r}
cr_get_ratio("#A4DBE8", "#EBEBEB")
```

:::

## Consideration: Make your graphs accessible!

Use white space to help separate elements.

```{r, fig.width= 13, echo = FALSE, fig.asp=.4}
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2, fill = dplyr)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "seq", palette = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

p2 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2, fill = dplyr)) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(type = "seq", palette = 1)  +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
p1 + p2
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Consideration: Make your graphs accessible!

Use a large enough font size!  

```{r, fig.width= 13, echo = FALSE, fig.asp=.5}
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#A71F69", color = "white") +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip()

p2 <- ggplot(data = math241_form, mapping = aes(x = ggplot2)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#A71F69", color = "white") +
  labs(x = "ggplot2 Experience",
       y = "Number of students") +
  coord_flip() + theme(text = element_text(size = 10))
p1 + p2
```

## Data Viz Considerations

* We could spend all semester on data viz principles.

::: {.fragment}

* Be thoughtful and iterate.  

:::

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

* Let's spend some time considering the strengths and weaknesses of some graphs via an [activity](../in_class/activity1.qmd).
    + Pick out the:
        + Clearest story
        + Most memorable
        + Best overall

:::

* Be ready to present one of your graphs to the class, if we have time.

```{r}
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(15)
```
